summary: This bill directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to identify and review evidence-based interventions, best practices, curricula, and staff trainings that improve the social-emotional and behavioral health of children and support staff wellness in Head Start programs, and then awards grants to Head Start agencies to implement these interventions.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly authorizes an appropriation of $100,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2036 to fund grants, evaluations, and Best Practice Centers related to early childhood mental health interventions in Head Start programs. This directly increases government spending.

The bill focuses on identifying, implementing, and evaluating interventions to improve the behavioral health and social-emotional development of children in Head Start programs, with a clear link to later mental health outcomes. This directly relates to healthcare, specifically mental health services for children.

The bill targets interventions within Head Start and Early Head Start programs, which are federal programs designed to promote school readiness for children from low-income families. By enhancing these programs with mental health support, it strengthens a component of the social safety net.

The bill is entirely focused on Head Start and Early Head Start programs, which are educational programs for young children. It aims to improve the social-emotional and behavioral health of children within these educational settings, directly impacting early childhood education.
